newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo replaces turnover tax with value-added tax.
newsitem.headline: Congo replaces turnover tax with value-added tax.

text.p: Congo introduced a value-added tax (VAT) of 18 percent on June 1, to replace a turnover tax that had been levied at 17 percent.
Finance Minister Nguila Moungounga said the move would simplify and modernise the West African country's fiscal system, "for the good of its economy as well as of consumers".
Unlike the turnover tax, the VAT can be offset against taxes on company profits.
It will not be levied on basic foodstuffs like bread and milk, nor on locally-grown fruit and vegetables, nor on newspapers, newsprint and medicines.
"If the prices of these things went up, it would be pure speculation, punishable by the law, since technically that cannot be justified," Moungounga said.

The introduction of value-added tax is part of the tax and customs reforms being undertaken by the six countries of the Central African customs and economic union (UDEAC) -- Congo, Gabon, Central African Republic, Cameroon, Chad and Equatorial Guinea. Cameroon and Gabon have already introduced the tax.
